title: FizzBuzz
description: Solve the classic FizzBuzz problem — print numbers 1-20 with Fizz for multiples of 3, Buzz for multiples of 5, and FizzBuzz for both.

steps.title: Print numbers 1 to 20
steps.description: Use a `for` loop to print the numbers 1 through 20 to the console, each on its own line.
hints: A for loop: for (let i = 1; i <= 20; i++)

verification.failureMessage: Make sure you print each number from 1 to 20.

steps.title: Fizz for multiples of 3
steps.description: Inside the loop, print `"Fizz"` instead of the number when the number is divisible by 3.
hints: Use if (i % 3 === 0) to check divisibility by 3
Print "Fizz" for multiples of 3, otherwise print the number

verification.failureMessage: Multiples of 3 should show 'Fizz' instead of the number.

steps.title: Buzz for multiples of 5
steps.description: Print `"Buzz"` instead of the number when the number is divisible by 5.
hints: Use else if (i % 5 === 0) to check multiples of 5
Check divisibility by 3 FIRST, then by 5
Numbers that are multiples of both 3 and 5 will still show Fizz

verification.failureMessage: Multiples of 5 should show 'Buzz' instead of the number.

steps.title: FizzBuzz for both
steps.description: Print `"FizzBuzz"` when a number is divisible by both 3 and 5. The FizzBuzz check must come first!
hints: Check i % 3 === 0 && i % 5 === 0 as the FIRST condition
If both, print "FizzBuzz", not the number
15 is the first number divisible by both 3 and 5 in this range

verification.successMessage: FizzBuzz appears for numbers divisible by both 3 and 5!
verification.failureMessage: Make sure FizzBuzz appears and numbers like 15 don't.

steps.title: Refactor as a function
steps.description: Refactor the logic into a `fizzbuzz(n)` function that returns the result for a single number, then call it from a loop.
hints: The function should return "FizzBuzz", "Fizz", "Buzz", or the number as a string
Use the function inside the loop: console.log(fizzbuzz(i))
The function makes the code reusable and testable

verification.successMessage: The refactored function produces the same output! Reusable code is clean code.
verification.failureMessage: Make sure fizzbuzz(15) returns 'FizzBuzz' and the loop output is correct.
